transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I'm really struggling with my eating habits lately and felt like I needed to seek help. I keep having these episodes where I eat massive amounts of food in a very short period of time, and I feel completely unable to stop once I start. It's getting really out of hand and is making me very distressed.

After these episodes, do you ever try to make up for the eating by vomiting, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising a lot? This will help me understand what kind of eating problem you’re dealing with.

It's really hard to admit, but yes, I do those things because I get so panicked about the food I've eaten. After a big episode, I force myself to throw up and sometimes take laxatives to get it out of my system. I also try to fast the next day or force myself to exercise for hours to make up for it.
Have you been at a significantly low body weight for your age and height, or has your weight stayed in the normal or higher range?
I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. My weight fluctuates a lot because of all this, but I don't think it has ever been significantly low.
Is your body shape or weight something that strongly affects how you feel about yourself or causes an intense fear of gaining weight?

Yes, absolutely. My entire self-worth is completely tied to the number on the scale and how my body looks, and I feel like an absolute failure if I gain any weight. I have this constant, terrifying fear of becoming fat that completely consumes my thoughts every day.
Outside of the binge episodes, do you regularly restrict how much you eat to the point that your weight has dropped well below what is expected for your height and age?
I do sometimes fast and restrict my food intake to try to prevent weight gain. However, I don't think my weight has ever dropped to a level that is well below what is expected for my height and age.
